title: Learn business through stories
header_line: My analysis of one book on an entrepreneur's life. Not a summary of the book. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the author or publisher.

lines.text: What business idea did you only understand once someone told it as a story?

Coming from a literature background, I said, I would pick up business books and go: oh my God, I don't even understand what they are talking about. I would look at what people were reading who read about finance and accounting, and get lost in dense texts.
I spent more time going back and forth to the dictionary than reading, I said. I would get ten pages into a textbook and give up.

Then I decided to read literature about business: stories about entrepreneurs. I can totally understand the train of thought, I said. I can understand the journey. I'm understanding the terms because they're in context to a larger story.
What a great way to teach business, I said: by telling the stories. You identify with a story, and you learn the terms as you live the career. What is equity? What is a reverse merger?
In this book I now see many lessons. You can see how the person goes from childhood to being a successful entrepreneur, and the tiny moments that opened up the rest of his life.

If we can identify the defining moments in our own life, I said, then we can say: this is a decision I need to make. A lot of people fail at being entrepreneurs because they just don't make the decision.
What decision are you putting off, and what story would help you see it?

exercise.title: Five minutes
steps: Write a business term you did not understand until you saw it in a story.
Write the story that made it clear.
Write one defining moment in your life that you could turn into a story.
Write one decision you are putting off.
Write one story you will read or listen to this week.

check.q: Where did I say the business terms made sense to me?
choices: In the context of a larger story

check.q: What did I say a lot of people fail at as entrepreneurs?
What can we do with defining moments in our own life, I said?
choices: Identify them, to see which decision we need to make

recap: Learn through stories. Name your defining moments, then make the decision.
